text:
alex: FYI i hit a bundler edge case with our JS SDK. only fails when a consumer does a dynamic import inside an edge worker + the package uses conditional exports. repro across vite, rollup, webpack.

chen: yikes. can you share the tiny repro & error?

alex: minimal structure: package.json has conditional exports: 
{
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
    }
  },
  "type": "module"
}
app code (edge worker): `export default async () => { const sdk = await import('my-sdk'); return sdk.createClient(); }`

sam: what's the runtime error from the edge bundle?

alex: vite dev: `TypeError: Cannot set property 'exports' of #<Object> at __toCommonJS...`
webpack prod: `Module not found: Can't resolve './dist/esm/index.js'` even though file exists in node_modules/my-sdk/dist/esm.

maria: that smells like the bundler resolver ignoring `exports` conditional during pre-resolution. dynamic import triggers static resolution at build time and some resolvers pick the wrong export path.

chen: did you try importing the explicit file `my-sdk/dist/esm/index.js`?

alex: yes that makes vite/rollup happy but webpack still sometimes pulls CJS variant in and the runtime glue breaks in edge. repro repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-packaging/edge-dyn-import (small). commands: `npm i && npm run build:vite|rollup|webpack`.

build-bot: note: our edge bundler pipeline rewrites `import()` to loader wrappers; webpack's resolver uses `mainFields` order which can cause module vs exports mismatch.

sam: probable causes: 1) bundlers perform package resolution without honoring conditional `exports` qualifiers for edge targets, 2) `type: "module"` + coexisting CJS artefacts can confuse emit helpers.

maria: another vector — TypeScript types: `types` is declared but not surfaced in `exports`, so editors can't map bare import to d.ts. we should add `"exports": { "./package.json": { "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts" } }` or use `typesVersions`.

chen: repro idea: add a non-conditional alias entry like `"exports": { ".": "./dist/esm/index.js", ... }` and see if bundlers pick it. also test setting webpack `resolve.mainFields` to `['module','main']`.

alex: tried adding a top-level plain `"."` string pointing to esm — fixes vite & rollup; webpack needed explicit `mainFields` tweak. changing `type` to remove module helps webpack but breaks node consumers.

sam: short-term workaround we used in prod: include a `browser` key in exports mapping: `"browser": "./dist/esm/index.js"` — instructs browser/edge bundlers to prefer ESM.

maria: sounds reasonable as stopgap. long-term we should update our SDK publish script to emit `exports` with explicit `browser` and `types` entries, plus add a `module` field and ensure `dist/esm` is resolvable without relying only on conditionals.

chen: i'll add a test-case to our bundler CI: create a tiny edge worker that dynamic-imports the package and run build across webpack/vite/rollup. i'll experiment with `resolve.mainFields` and `resolve.conditionNames` in webpack.

alex: i've pushed /tests/{webpack,vite,rollup}-edge configs and build logs to the repro. also included the failing bundle snippets in tests/notes.md.

sam: i'll draft a short devex doc: "Edge packaging checklist: exports, browser map, types" — include minimal package.json templates and recommended ship-time checks.

maria: add a note on typings resolution and editors — example for `exports` with `types` exposure. i'll review the doc.

achen: (typo) will post webpack findings later today.

alex: thanks all. marking this thread resolved after the docs PR lands. :thumbsup:
